display.title: Hashem Knows How to Help You, Part 1
display.summary_short: What it means to 'throw' our burden onto Hashem, and the story of Reb Shmuel Brin, a distillery owner falsely accused, who comes to the Rebbe Maharash for help.
display.summary_long: The storyteller explains the difference between believing in Hashem and trusting in Him: trust means being as relaxed as someone walking near a cliff with eyes closed, held by a friend. He explains Dovid HaMelech's words in Tehillim, 'Cast your burden upon Hashem': when we throw something we let go completely, so true bitachon means handing over a problem and no longer worrying how Hashem will solve it. Then the story begins. Reb Shmuel Brin, a Chassid of the Rebbe Maharash who owns a vodka distillery, arrives in Lubavitch unexpectedly. Two of his workers secretly drained vodka from the tank, and when one was caught, he told the police that his boss had ordered it to avoid taxes. Now Shmuel faces trial and possible exile to Siberia. The Rebbe Maharash tells him that 'from where will my help come' can also mean 'help comes from nowhere', and instructs him to help fully any Jew who says those words to him. Shmuel then hears that his friend Chaim's riverside inn has burned down, and goes to help. To be continued.
display.lesson: True bitachon means letting go of our worries and trusting Hashem to help in His own way, even out of nowhere.

advisories.note: A Jew is falsely accused and expects hostile judges; he faces possible exile to Siberia.
Two workers get into a fistfight; a friend's inn burns down (no one hurt).

characters: Reb Shmuel Brin, the distillery owner
